guarantees.claim: mul_a0_b_inv is continuously assigned to the GF(2^4) product of a0 and b_inv_buf via aes_mul_gf2p4.
mul_m0_b_inv is continuously assigned to the GF(2^4) product of m0 and b_inv_buf via aes_mul_gf2p4.
mul_a1_b2_inv is continuously assigned to the GF(2^4) product of a1 and b2_inv via aes_mul_gf2p4.
mul_m1_b2_inv is continuously assigned to the GF(2^4) product of m1 and b2_inv via aes_mul_gf2p4.

assumptions.claim: Inputs a0, m0, b_inv_buf, a1, m1, b2_inv are stable GF(2^4) values when read by the continuous assignments.
assumptions.risk: glitches or invalid GF(2^4) encodings could produce incorrect products and break the masked inverse computation.

uncertain_points.claim: The comment warns against aggressive synthesis optimizations that could merge multiplier outputs sharing inputs, potentially leaking side-channel information by undermining the masked implementation.
uncertain_points.risk: If the synthesis tool merges these multiplication paths, the physical separation of masked terms is lost, enabling first-order side-channel attacks.
